slurm_mapping_determination.the_trap: The markers for res_boot_1 and res_boot_2 name jobs 57252343 and 57252344 -- neither of which appears in the handoff's candidate list, and neither of which is an array job. Grepping the three markers for '57252337' finds ONE of three and would look like a two-thirds mismatch. It is not: the marker's `job` field records SLURM_JOB_ID (the per-task RAW job id), not SLURM_ARRAY_JOB_ID. Slurm assigns each array task its own raw id and only ONE task inherits the array base, which is why exactly one marker per member cites the array id.
slurm_mapping_determination.resolution: sacct --format=JobID,JobIDRaw maps 57252337_1 -> raw 57252343 and 57252337_2 -> raw 57252344. Both markers are therefore consistent with array job 57252337.

manifest_row.why_open_and_not_generated: generate_manifest.py coerces any un-overridden path under docs/orchestration/state/ to MACHINE/generated (:371-374), and derive_immutable(:239-241) then returns immutable=yes. That coercion is correct for GENERATOR OUTPUT and wrong here on OI-73's own stated grounds -- 'a GENERATED run/state record is immutable evidence; an AUTHORED input under those trees is not'. This file is hand-authored; no script in the tree emits it. Two concrete reasons `open` is the right call rather than a formality: (1) the destination carries an explicitly disclosed, explicitly UNCLOSED residual -- pscratch is purged -- and when a durability copy is authorized, this receipt is where it must be recorded; immutable=yes would reproduce exactly the OI-73 deadlock in which the one file able to clear a blocker is the one no lane may touch. (2) Mutability costs nothing in evidentiary strength here, because every load-bearing field is independently recomputable: the six sha256 values can be re-derived from the quarantined files, and the Slurm identities from sacct. A reader does not have to trust this file's bytes.
